'''Daniel Kastler''' ({{IPA|fr|kastlɛʁ|lang}}; 4 March 1926 – 4 July 2015)<ref>{{cite web|title=Décès de Daniel Kastler|url=https://smf.emath.fr/actualites-smf/deces-de-daniel-kastler|website=smf.emath.fr|access-date=March 2, 2021|language=fr}}</ref> was a French theoretical [[physicist]], working on the foundations of [[quantum field theory]] and on [[non-commutative geometry]]. He is known as the co-developer of the [[Kadison–Kastler metric]] and the [[Algebraic quantum field theory#Haag–Kastler axioms|Haag–Kastler axioms]].

== Biography ==
Daniel Kastler was born on March 4, 1926, in [[Colmar]], a city in the [[Haut-Rhin]] [[département]] in north-eastern France. He was the son of the 1966 Physics [[Nobel Prize]] laureate [[Alfred Kastler]]. In 1946 he enrolled at the [[École Normale Superieure]] in [[Paris]]. In 1950 he moved to Germany and became [[lecturer]] at the [[Saarland University]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Lazzarini|first1 = Serge|last2 = Martin|first2 = Thierry |title = Daniel Kastler 1926–2015|journal = CERN Courier|page = 40|year = 2015|volume = 55|number = 8|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/2232500/files/vol55-issue8-p037-e.pdf}}</ref> In 1953, he was promoted to [[associate professor]] and obtained a doctorate in [[quantum chemistry]]. In 1957 Kastler moved to the [[University of Aix-Marseille]] and became a [[full professor]] in 1959. In 1968 he founded, together with [[Jean-Marie Souriau]] and Andrea Visconti, the Center of Theoretical Physics in [[Marseille]].<ref>The center is known as ''Centre de Physique Théorique'' of Marseille.</ref><ref>{{cite web|last = Guichardet|first = Alain|language = fr|title = Quelques souvenirs sur Daniel Kastler (1926-2015)|url = https://smf.emath.fr/sites/default/files/old_site/kastler.pdf|website = smf.emath.fr|access-date = March 2, 2021}}</ref> Daniel Kastler died on July 8, 2015, in [[Bandol]], in southern France.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kastler obituary|url=https://www.i2m.univ-amu.fr/IMG/article_PDF/Disparitions-du-math-maticien-danois-Uffe-Haagerup_a715.pdf|website=University of Aix-Marseille|date=9 July 2015|access-date=February 28, 2021|archive-date=16 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016081821/https://www.i2m.univ-amu.fr/IMG/article_PDF/Disparitions-du-math-maticien-danois-Uffe-Haagerup_a715.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Lazzarini|first1 = Serge|last2 = Martin|first2 = Thierry |title = Daniel Kastler (1926–2015)|journal = News Bulletin, International Association of Mathematical Physics|pages = 27–28|year = 2015|url = https://www.iamp.org/bulletins/old-bulletins/Bulletin-July2015-print.pdf}}</ref>

Daniel Kastler is known in particular for his work with [[Rudolf Haag]] on the foundation of the algebraic approach to quantum field theory. Their collaboration started at the famous Lille Conference in 1957, where both were present, and culminated in the Haag–Kastler axioms<ref>In the 2000s the original paper was one of the [https://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/topcites/older/topcites/alltime.mathphys.2.shtml most cited papers in mathematical physics]. {{Cite journal|last1 = Haag|first1 = Rudolf|last2 = Kastler|first2 = Daniel|title = An Algebraic approach to quantum field theory|journal = Journal of Mathematical Physics|volume = 5|pages = 848–861|year = 1964|issue = 7|doi = 10.1063/1.1704187|bibcode = 1964JMP.....5..848H}}</ref> for local observables of quantum field theories. This framework uses elements of the theory of [[operator algebra]]s and is therefore referred to as [[algebraic quantum field theory]] or, from the physical point of view, as [[local quantum physics]].<ref>{{Cite book|last = Haag|first = Rudolf|date = 1996|edition = 2|title = Local quantum physics: Fields, particles, algebras|publisher = Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg|isbn =  978-3-540-61049-6|doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-61458-3}}</ref> In other collaborations, Kastler showed the importance of [[C*-algebra]]s in the foundations of [[quantum statistical mechanics]] and in abelian asymptotic systems.<ref>{{cite web|last = Guichardet|first = Alain|title = Daniel Kastler et les Systèmes dynamiques non commutatifs|url = https://smf.emath.fr/sites/default/files/old_site/dk.pdf|website = smf.emath.fr|language = fr|access-date = March 2, 2021}}</ref> In the 1980s he started working on [[Alain Connes]]' non-commutative geometry, especially studying the applications in [[elementary particle physics]].<ref>{{cite web|last = Connes|first = Alain|title = Daniel Kastler|url = https://noncommutativegeometry.blogspot.com/2015/07/daniel-kastler.html|website = noncommutativegeometry.blogspot.com| date=18 July 2015 |access-date = March 2, 2021}}</ref> In the same period Kastler, in collaboration with [[Raymond Stora]], developed the geometrical setting for the [[BRST quantization|BRST transformations]] for the quantization of [[gauge theory|gauge theories]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Daniel Kastler 1926-2015|journal = La Gazette|pages = 70–71|year = 2015|number = 146|url = http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/2015/146/smf_gazette_146_70-71.pdf|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171209130416/http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/2015/146/smf_gazette_146_70-71.pdf|archive-date = 2017-12-09|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kastler|first1=Daniel|last2=Stora|first2=Raymond|title=A differential geometric setting for BRS transformations and anomalies. 1.|journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics|volume=3|page=437|year=1986|issue=4|doi=10.1016/0393-0440(86)90006-9|bibcode=1986JGP.....3..437K}} {{Cite journal|last1=Kastler|first1=Daniel|last2=Stora|first2=Raymond|title=A differential geometric setting for BRS transformations and anomalies. 2.|journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics|volume=3|pages=483–505|year=1986|issue=4|doi=10.1016/0393-0440(86)90007-0|bibcode=1986JGP.....3..483K}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1984 Daniel Kastler was awarded the [[Prix Ampère]] of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|title=40 ans du prix Ampère|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/prix/ampere_181016.pdf|language=fr|website=Académie des Sciences|access-date=February 28, 2021}}</ref> Since 1977 he was a corresponding member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences]]<ref>
{{cite web|url=https://adw-goe.de/en/members/personendetails/person/Daniel-Kastler/|language=de|title=Göttingen Academy of Sciences member page of Daniel Kastler|website=Göttingen Academy of Sciences|access-date=March 3, 2021}} {{cite book|date = 2011|title = Jahrbuch der Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen 2010|editor = Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen|publisher = De Gruyter|isbn = 978-3110236767|language=de|doi = 10.26015/adwdocs-386|author1 = (:Unkn) Unknown}}</ref> and since 1981 of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/m/kastler-daniel|title=Austrian Academy of Sciences member page of Daniel Kastler|website=Austrian Academy of Sciences|access-date=February 28, 2021}}</ref> Since 1995 he was a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/daniel-kastler/|title=German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina member page of Daniel Kastler|website=German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|access-date=February 28, 2021}}</ref>
